question: Which law states that endothermic animals from cold climates have smaller extremities or appendages than closely related species from warm climates?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Allen's rule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Allen's rule** is a biological principle that explains how the body shapes and sizes of endotherms vary with climate.
 
• It states that endothermic animals from colder climates generally have shorter extremities or appendages compared to those from warmer climates.
 
• This adaptation helps reduce heat loss in cold environments by minimizing the surface area to volume ratio.
 
• Allen's rule is named after the American zoologist **Joel Asaph Allen**, who first formulated this rule in 1877.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Endothermic Animals:**

 
 
• Endothermic animals, also known as warm-blooded animals, are those that maintain a constant body temperature independent of the environment.
 
• Examples include mammals and birds.
 
• These animals have metabolic mechanisms to generate heat when it is cold and to dissipate heat when it is hot.
 
 
 
• **Adaptation to Climate:**
 
 
• Adaptations are traits that have evolved through natural selection, allowing organisms to better survive and reproduce in their environments.
 
• In cold climates, endothermic animals develop shorter limbs, ears, and tails to conserve heat.
 
• In contrast, in warm climates, longer extremities help with heat dissipation.
 
 
 
• **Other Biological Rules:**
 
 
• **Bergmann's Rule:** States that within a broadly distributed taxonomic group, larger-sized species are found in colder environments, and smaller-sized species are found in warmer ones.
 
• **Gloger's Rule:** States that dark pigments increase in animals living in warm and humid habitats.
